expo.name: CFPI — Coastal & Flood Protection Inspection

extra.//: Where CFPI looks for FRCDE, baked into the published bundle so a colleague opening the shared link only has to sign in. No trailing slash. Settings still overrides it on-device for local development.

//runtimeVersion: The string Expo Go matches on. Publish with `npm run publish:demo`, which
pins eas-cli to 16.12.0 — do not publish with a newer one.
Expo Go decides whether it can run an update by comparing its own SDK against
the update's runtime version, in the form `exposdk:<sdk>`. eas-cli 22 ignores
the value below and rewrites this file on every publish to
`{ policy: 'appVersion' }`, which resolves to `1.0.0` — a runtime version no
Expo Go will ever match. 16.12.0 honours it and leaves the file alone.
The failure that causes is invisible from the terminal: the publish reports
success and prints a working dashboard link, while the update server answers
Expo Go with 204 No Content and the app never loads. Verify a publish by what
it served, not by what it printed:
npx eas-cli@16.12.0 update:list --branch demo    # expect exposdk:54.0.0
Change this when the SDK moves — and only alongside `eas build`, which is the
point at which Expo Go stops being how this app is distributed.
